projects.name: 1.2.2.2 - Towards sustainable energy for all: market-based dissemination of integrated renewable energy systems for productive activities in rural areas
projects.description:
Through its 3 technical components, the project will support the market-based adoption of integrated renewable energy systems (solar PV for irrigation and waste-to-energy) in small to medium-scale farms and rural agro-food processing industries in Mozambique. The components are the following: 
i. Establishment of a conducive policy and regulatory environment - the project will enhance the regulatory and policy environment in order to promote the involvement of the private sector in the development of integrated RE systems for rural areas. 
ii. Capacity building and knowledge management- the project will improve and develop the capabilities and knowledge of market players and enablers in the RE sector, including relevant government officials (national and provincial level) as well as representatives from financial institutions, private sector, universities and vocational training institutions. 
iii. Technology demonstration and scaling up - the project will demonstrate the technical and financial feasibility of RE technologies in agricultural activities located in rural areas, specifically: solar PV water pumping and biogas/biomass usage in agro-food processing industries through the installation of demonstration projects. The objectives of these projects, besides delivering GHG emission reductions, include generating case studies and best practices on the use of RE technologies in agro-food processing industries that have high replication potential across Mozambique

projects.name: 4.1.2.1 - Conservation of Globally Threatened Species (IWT)
projects.description:
While conservation efforts have been significantly up-scaled in Mozambique since the end of the civil war in 1992, there are several threats affecting biodiversity. Significant increase in wildlife crime has taken place, adding to the pressures caused by uncontrolled subsistence hunting by poor communities. Since 2014 the poaching has increased, targeting not only elephants but additional threatened species, such as lions, pangolins and other. The international market for wildlife products is still of low risk and highly profitable. Subsistence poaching also threatens a wide variety of globally endangered species.  With local communities expanding further into conservation areas and growing populations in need of food and income, the threats to wildlife and forest resources accelerate at alarming rates, nullifying conservation gains of recent years. 
The proposed project Objective is to strengthen the conservation of globally threatened species in Mozambique through implementation of the Conservation Areas Act – improving biodiversity enforcement and expanding protected areas through community conservancies and targeted rural development action.

The Expected Accomplishments (EAs) are:
EA1. A network of support platforms to reduce the vulnerability to climate hazards has been established within Beira’s surrounding area of influence, including resilient housing and community infrastructure (re)construction.
EA2. Livelihoods of targeted vulnerable communities and capacities of project stakeholders have been enhanced during the (re)construction process, preparing for scaling-up.
It is estimated that the project will support approximately 30,000 to 40,000 direct beneficiaries.

projects.name: 2.3.3.17 - INTEGRATED MULTI-SECTOR RESPONSE TO PROTRACTED HUMANITARIAN NEEDS FOR CYCLONE AFFECTED POPULATIONS IN MOZAMBIQUE
projects.description:
The objective of the project is to address the persisting and protracted humanitarian needs while preparing cyclone affected communities and individuals to build back safer in order to withstand potential disasters shocks. In order to contribute to this objective, IOM will implement the four programme components in an integrated manner to enhance synergies across sectors and enhancing the value for money of the overall strategy.

Outcome 1: Affected households with exceptionally high levels of cyclone damage have access to more disaster resilient shelter
Central: IOM will support 500 households in Chibabava resettlements sites, where no other shelter partners are responding and have therefore been identified as the most critical sites. Technical trainings and construction support will be provided to enable families of improving their shelter conditions. The shelter interventions will target 500 households each of whom will receive a voucher with a value of USD 600 (MZN 38,000). 
Northern; The shelter response will target communities in Cabo Delgado and Nampula, based on a selection criterion that includes damage extent, household vulnerability, coverage/gap analysis. The main goal is to promote durable solutions while optimizing and promoting the adequate use of locally available materials such as soil, lime, coconut wood from the fallen trees. In this effort, IOM will provide materials, training, orientation and supervision for the construction and reinforcement of houses. Approximately 500 households will be reached 

Outcome 2 – Improved living conditions and service provision (CCCM) for affected households in resettlements sites and host communities 
Central: In line with the critical CCCM Cluster Coordination support role in country IOM will focus on capacity building and supporting local authorities in the coordination of services across 2 provinces (5 districts- Dombe, Buzi, Nhamatanda, Chibabava, Dondo)., IOM will provide support to community-based site development committees to identify and implement community defined prioritized site development projects. In prioritized sites, IOM will address critical site planning and stabilisation challenges faced by people in resettlement areas, including drainage, access road clearance, plot demarcations. 
Northern: Maintaining an integrated approach, approach and in line with the CCCM Cluster Coordination support role in country, IOM will provide support to local authorities in the coordination of humanitarian assistance and monitoring of service provision as well as needs assessment and analysis in Memba, Nampula Province as well as two sites in Cabo Delgado. In coordination with the shelter teams, the CCCM activities will ensure construction of communal space facilities in the three identified resettlement areas of Memba. In order to support displaced populations in hard to reach areas, IOM will provide technical staff including engineers and site planners to support the government efforts on land demarcation in resettlement areas.

Outcome 3: Reduced protection risks and improved psychosocial well-being for cyclone and conflict-affected populations 
Central: A gender balanced protection/MHPSS team, composed by 3 Protection Focal Points and 2 psychologists (integrated into the CCCM Mobile teams) will conduct protection activities in a total of 27 prioritized resettlement sites (Dondo, Nhamatanda and Buzi Districts in Sofala Province and Sussundenga District in Manica Province) and supervise the work of 27 community social workers in the protection desks. MHPSS activities will be conducted in six prioritized resettlement sites, three in each province.
Northern: IOM will continue to operate integrated (Health/Protection/MHPSS) mobile teams constituted by gender-balanced, locally-hired members from the districts and communities they work at. Following internal trainings in referral pathways, protection concerns, psychological first aid, among other related themes. IOM teams will also provide psychosocial support services. 

Outcome 4: – Humanitarian actors and government have access to accurate and timely displacement data to support informed coordination and response planning
DTM will conduct two methodologies – (i) mobility tracking and (ii) surveys. The aim is to provide a comprehensive overview of the situation with regards to internal displacement and IDPs living conditions.

projects.name: 3.1.1.2 - Capacity Building Support to Mozambican Authorities and Assistance to Potentially At-Risk Groups in Marginalized Communities in Mozambique to Addressing Violent Extremism
projects.description:
Violent extremism is a growing threat in the Cabo Delgado province of Mozambique, causing displacement and creating a climate of fear and distrust in communities. 

The project aims to build resilience to violent extremist influences in Cabo Delgado by understanding and addressing socio-economic needs in affected communities. It includes four core components of intervention: i) research, ii) individual assistance, iii) community assistance and iv) government capacity building. 
The research component will identify the areas of origin and driving factors for persons recruited into or otherwise joining violent extremist groups and inform targeted programming. 

Second, at the individual level, the project will provide a range of employment, training and income generation services intended to create sustainable livelihoods to up to 1000 beneficiaries and their dependents. Participants will engage in counselling sessions to develop employment plans and counsellors will refer participants to any relevant services needed (health, including psychosocial support, legal, housing, etc.). 

Third, at the community level, marginalized communities where the target beneficiaries are residing will be supported through the implementation of a Community Revitalization Project (CRP) whereby community members, through selected representatives, will identify initiatives aimed to address community needs. The CRP approach is designed to encourage community participation and ownership of the process.
 
Finally, the capacity building component will focus on the establishment and provision of on-going technical support to community-level structures.

projects.description:
Idai Affected Areas
Procure and distribute ‘return’ shelter kits and NFIs to 4,000 households (20,000 individuals) to facilitate their return to communities of origin
CCCM Site improvement and site decommissioning. IOM will support improvements in 10 collective displacement sites (inclusive of the 5 sites established by IOM in Figure 2) identified as most in need of support by IOM’s CCCM experts and in close coordination with INGC and the CCCM Task Force. IOM will deploy of DTM/CCCM Site Facilitation Teams, when required, to enhance site management and support (SMS), coordination, accountability, and information management to support the delivery of humanitarian services to IDPs in displacement sites and return areas across central Mozambique including Beira (Sofala), Tete, Manica and Zambezia. 
The Displacement Tracking Matrix will scale up operations to provide a comprehensive baseline of displacement and return locations across Sofala, Manica, Zambezia, and Tete, in collaboration with INGC and humanitarian partners. IOM will improve the availability of timely and accurate information about the needs of IDPs 
IOM MHPSS intervention will reach a total of 1,500 beneficiaries assisted and cared through a minimum of 3,000 services in transit centers, areas of relocation and affected communities of Buzi and Nhamatanda Districts (Sofala Province). 50 professionals among paramedical staff, social workers and volunteers of partners organizations will receive training and coaching sessions to provide community-based psychosocial support. 
The project will also assist in the referral and transfer of patients and displaced persons requiring medical care, in Buzi and Dondo, Sofala province. Through a referral and discharge service, the project will contribute to reducing morbidity and mortality among cyclone survivors by increasing access to medical care and facilitating referrals for the most vulnerable. The project will target persons the critically injured, children, elderly, women (pregnant and lactating), people with disabilities, HIV and TB patients living in temporary and resettlement sites and communities of return. 
Up to 4,000 hygiene kits inclusive of soap soap, sanitary items, and household water purifications will be purchased and distributed amongst the most vulnerable displaced populations to complement other partners first hygiene kit’s distributions. Hygiene promotion sessions/materials will be carried out in camp/sites.

Kennet Affected Areas

IOM will provide four partners with support to procure cluster recommended shelter kits and other shelter supplies inclusive of transportation, distribution costs and operational costs. The procurement will include items identified as critical to ensure timely repair and associated restoration of living conditions for affected persons, as well as a restricted number of prioritized materials that may be pre-identified by the Shelter and NFI Cluster.
The kits will include tarpaulins, shelter toolkits and some key additional construction materials such as fixings like nails, rope and wire so affected households are independently enabled to rebuild and construct new shelters. Furthermore, the kits will also include solar lamps which are not only critical in a context where the power supply may be affected, but also for the safe movement of persons, especially vulnerable persons, at all times.
Under this action, IOM will closely work with INGC and the Province Directorate for Gender, Children and Social Action (DPGCAS) as well as the protection cluster in order to adapt and re-activate adequate referral pathways for vulnerable persons, including people with disabilities, unaccompanied and separated children and those who are at risk of or might have become victims of violence, including Trafficking in Persons (TiP) and Gender-based Violence (GBV). The referral pathways are based on a contingency plan for protection in emergencies, which was developed in partnership with the Government and UNICEF and has successfully been activated in Sofala following the Idai cyclone.
IOM will implement protection and safety audits at displacement sites as well as a protection monitoring amongst affected population in order to strengthen the understanding of to what extent child migration and child labour might be used as coping strategies by affected families. In line with the findings of the protection monitoring, IOM will design and disseminate specific messages to address the phenomenon and to inform families and communities about the risks related to such a practice. It will also inform communities about existing support and social protection structures that will support families and communities in coping with the negative effects of the hazard.

projects.description:
The proposed CERF project will contribute to respond to the priority shelter/NFI, protection and CCCM needs of 50,200 IDPs, through:

Shelter/NFI: The displaced populations and their host communities are in urgent need of emergency shelter support, as well as essential household items in order to secure safe, dignified, and healthy living conditions that provide at least basic protection from further adversities. Therefore, the project will aim to cover approximately 30,000 individuals (6,000 households) over a period of 6 months through the provision of emergency shelter items. The emergency shelter materials targeting will be based on shelter need assessments and which will enable each family to build a basic shelter or repair or rehabilitate an existing structure. The shelter kits for 4,000 families included in this proposal are based on extensive engagement with displaced families and their host communities across the province. The objective is to enable access to more dignified and adequate shelter for the displaced families – to reduce the need (and risk) of IDPs to be in “debt” to host families, obliged to repay with “favours” that pose a risk for exploitation and abuse, including sexual exploitation.



Protection, including Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS): Building on IOM’s existing experience and human resource capacities on the ground, leveraging IOM’s protection and MHPSS footprint to respond to the humanitarian needs of conflict affected populations, the CERF funds will support the strengthening of appropriate and comprehensive protection/MHPSS services and referrals at district level, from awareness-raising of target populations, identification of issues and cases, referrals and follow-up, and direct assistance in the provisionally earmarked districts of Macomia, Pemba and Mocimboa da Praia, with an outreach of 30,000 people and direct life-saving assistance to 200 people (50 direct and 150 referrals). It is to note however, and in coordination with the protection cluster members and especially UNHCR to avoid duplication of activities, that targeted district locations may change during the course of this programme as the situation remains dynamic and UNDSS guidelines as well as access to locations change due to security concerns or the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. a. projects.description:
This project is funded by the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID) through the CoM SSA initiative (Covenant of Mayor for South-Saharan Africa) funded by the European Union (EU) having as general aim to “increase the capacities of cities to provide access to sufficient, sustainable and safe energy related services to urban and peri-urban populations (especially the poor), with special attention to energy efficiency and renewable energy as drivers for local low emission, climate resilient, sustainable development”. This project is then part of a wider AECID-coordinated programme implemented in four African countries among which Mozambique in Maputo Metropolitan Area, with the name “Climate Change Mitigation through an Inclusive and Sustainable Mobility Model in the Maputo Metropolitan Area”. Besides UN-Habitat the other direct implementing partners and recipients are AMT and Maputo, Matola and Boane Municipality.  AMB, ASF, University Eduardo Mondlane (UEM) and WAZA (observatorio de transporte) will be also involved in activities implementation. 
The overall programme has a timeframe of 30 months and aims at contributing to mitigation and adaptation to climate change through implementation of measures for the sustainability of mobility and transport in Maputo Metropolitan Area and contributing to provide a metropolitan, inclusive and sustainable perspective into urban planning and management.
The majority of the programme activities will be addressed through this project, but other programme activities implemented by the donor and the above mentioned partners will complement this project in a synergic way. In particular with activities of AMT strengthening of technical and managing capacity through hiring of specialized technical staff to be integrated in the organigram of the institution and equipment provision; monitoring of air quality in Maputo Metropolitan Area etc.

Under this ‘umbrella’ Programme, this specific project will be implemented by the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) in close collaboration with Architects Without Border (ASF) and Barcelona Metropolitan Area (AMB) and always in coordination with the Maputo Metropolitan Transport Agency (AMT) and local Municipalities of the Maputo Metropolitan Area. 
Specifically, UN-Habitat has been collaborating for long time with AMB and ASF. AMB is a public institution with a model of a metropolitan management approach, and ASF is a Spanish NGO based in Maputo for more than 10 years tackling issues related to urban development and human rights.  
This project will be a joint action of these three partners, since each of them contribute with their own expertise complementing each other throughout the project.

projects.name: 1.2.1.2 - Development of a National Urban Policy
projects.description:
Urbanization is happening in almost the entire Mozambican territory. Cities and villages are growing faster than the Great Maputo area, according to the Census 2017 results. The main drivers of urbanisation are people looking for jobs and better living conditions; however, due to a dysfunctional urban system, urbanisation has not yet allowed reducing poverty. Hence, cities are still functioning more as poverty traps than generating opportunities for sustainable development. The World Bank study ‘Maputo Urban Poverty and Inclusive Growth’ from June 2017 brought evidence that poverty levels grow as distance from the Maputo city centre increases. 
A well-managed urbanisation will represent a concrete opportunity for Mozambique to increase investments in cities, creating jobs and accommodating in a sustainable manner the rapid population growth – in the last decade averaging almost 900,000 people per year. To address sustainable urban development, the Ministry of Public Works requested UN-Habitat to develop a study to justify the need for a National Urban Policy (NUP), which was concluded in February 2018.
 
According to this study and  and the conversations with the Government, the NUP will be a process lead by the Government. The key issues addressed by the NUP are as follow: (i) capturing and sharing urban land added-value to increase municipal revenues and promote more public investments; (ii) increasing densities and promoting social mix; (iii) increasing access to housing; (iv) simplifying and improving the planning framework, with a clear vision of future urban development; (v) integrating systematically risk management and resilience aspects in urban planning and management; (vi) strengthening rural-urban linkages; and (viii) promoting metropolitan management mechanisms between municipalities/districts across administrative borders.

projects.name: 4.2.2.22 - Building Resilience Through Education and Community engagement in the cyclone-affected schools in Mozambique ( EU IcPS)
projects.description:
According to the Global Climate Risk Index (2014), Mozambique is highly prone to natural disasters, and is the third most vulnerable country in Africa regarding cyclones, floods, droughts, tornadoes, epidemics and earthquakes of small magnitude. The education system in Mozambique has expanded considerably since the end of the civil war in 1992. Primary enrollment has more than tripled from 2000 to 2018, from just over 2 million to 6.5 million students in keeping with demographic pressures caused by population growth as well as commitments from the Millennium Development Goals, which rallied countries around universal access to basic education. However, rapid expansion of the system has meant trade-offs. There are obstacles to reinforcing existing building stock placed in disaster prone areas; parents and communities have built classrooms with local materials that cannot withstand the impact of the cyclical natural hazards. Thus, such structures suffer recurrent damage each year and pose a risk for the safety of children and teachers, all this underlines the need for stronger response to include safety standards during the recovery phase. This project aims to capitalize the efforts made by the MINEDH and the local communities of Sofala province to find improved solutions and safe learning spaces for children living in cyclone or flood prone areas  through adopting sustainable approaches that will break the vicious cycle of communities building schools that are then damaged in cyclical weather events, then rebuilt, then damaged and so on. 
Through this project, Mozambique  will pursue enhanced capacities to strengthen the resilience of children and communities in cyclone and flood affected areas through the design of adaptation options that are inclusive and gender transformative.

Insecurity and attacks against civilians across the Cabo Delgado province increased in late 2019 and early 2020, leading to a significant rise in displacement across the province, and a consequent increase in protection risks, for both displaced persons, host families and those left behind. The context has significantly changed since 2019 – the insecurity environment sharply deteriorated, physical access was further restricted, and the number of displaced population and humanitarian needs more than doubled from 65,000 in October 2019 to over 175,000 in April 2020. IOM currently estimates that more than 175,000 people (approx. 35,000 families) are displaced and in need of immediate assistance.  
 
Building IOM’s emergency response capacity that has reached more than 500,000 affected people to date, the proposed interventions will support the continuation and consolidation of an integrated and multi-sectoral approach with a strong emphasis on Protection, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), Shelter/non-food items (NFI), and Health. The response will target priority areas which have been identified based on vulnerability, needs and lack of partners’ presence. IOM’s response will address vulnerabilities induced by conflict and support preparedness and response to the CCOVID-19 pandemic which could exacerbate pre-existing challenges and vulnerabilities. The approach will engage the affected households and communities throughout the phase of implementation. 
 
IOM’s interventions will include: i) Contribution to the DTM operations in Northern Mozambique, ii) Integrated Health/MHPSS/Protection services, iii) Shelter/NFI support, and iv) COVID-19 Preparedness and response. IOM will continue coordination and advocacy through existing sectoral clusters, fully aligned with the current Humanitarian Response Plan running until May 2020 and the Rapid Response Plan for Cabo Delgado.

projects.name: 2.1.1.6 - Education can not wait in Cyclones and Flood affected communities in Mozambique
projects.description:
1.	Introduction
Cyclone Idai hit Mozambique on 14-15 March, leaving behind a swath of destruction in Gaza, Inhambane, Manica, Sofala, Tete, and Zambezia provinces. The hardest hit area is the coastal city of Beira in Sofala Province, 90% of infrastructure is estimated to have been destroyed. According to the World Bank, it estimated that the capital damages of buildings, infrastructure and agriculture amount to $656m- $773m . The Project aims to respond to immediate, emergency needs – getting children (aged 3- 18 years old) back into school and learning by: establishing temporary learning spaces, providing roofing for classrooms and through child-lead disaster risk reduction activities. This immediate phase will be dovetailed into and strategically linked with planning and investments for durable solutions in the form of quality, gender-sensitive rehabilitation efforts over the first 12 months following Cyclone Idai. 

2.	Main Objective
To integrate and deliver multi-sectoral education assistance to cyclone Idai affected children and communities, as well building local capacities to prepare for and respond to emergencies (DRR), contributing to reducing risk and vulnerabilities in districts of Sofala, Zambezia, Manica and Tete in Mozambique.
3.	Expected Accomplishments
EA1. 	Vulnerability of Flood and Cyclone affected classrooms is reduced by the rehabilitation according to safe learning environment standards (Building Back Better and Resilience) of MINEDH/UN Habitat.
EA2. 	Schools in affected areas comply with national standards of quality and safety with the focus on special needs for people with disabilities.
EA3. 	MINEDH at national and provincial levels has strengthened capacity to respond to emergencies through cluster coordination.

projects.name: 2.3.3.9 - Provision of Life-Saving Shelter and Food Assistance in Support of Cyclone and Flood Affected Communities in Cabo Delgado Province, Mozambique
projects.description: Tropical Cyclone Kenneth made landfall in Cabo Delgado province of northern Mozambique on 25 April with strong winds impacting several coastal areas. As of 28 April, 5 deaths and 11 injured have been reported, and 23,760 people have reportedly been displaced and are living in accommodation centers, according to the National Disaster Management Institute (INGC). At least 35,110 houses have been totally destroyed (3,805) or partially destroyed (31,305). The government reported that thousands of hectares of agricultural land have been destroyed, nearing and at harvest time, which will affect the food security in months to come. In responding to the impact of the floods and the urgent needs identified, IOM and WFP will seek to ensure affected populations in Cabo Delgado have access to lifesaving shelter and food assistance. An estimated 25,235 individuals will be reached under this action. In line with government priorities and request for assistance, the intervention will focus on the districts Macomia, Quissangua and Ibo, which have been severely impacted. Further government rapid assessments are underway, and geographical and beneficiary targeting might be adjusted as soon as more data becomes available. IOM will distribute Emergency Shelter Kits targeting the most vulnerable households of the affected population. IOM expects to reach 4,300 households with Emergency Shelter Assistance. WFP will implement as co-delegatee of IOM under this action. WFP, in collaboration with the authorities and food security cluster partners, will provide life-saving food assistance to populations in need. While the majority of life-saving food assistance will be provided through in-kind food assistance, in areas where markets will be proven to be functional and retailers will have sufficient capacity, WFP will make use of commodity vouchers to deliver food assistance. An estimated 5,047 households will be reached with food assistance.

projects.name: 2.3.2.12 - Promoting increased access to WASH, Information and Capacity for COVID 19 transmission prevention in the Informal Settlements of the Mozambican  Cities
projects.description:
It is clear that the pandemic will hit the Country’s most vulnerable people the hardest—many of them living in informal settlements and slums in cities. Mozambique is home to a large population of slum dwellers. About 80 percent of the Mozambican Urban Population lives in informal settlements. Recommended measures to prevent COVID-19 transmission such as hand washing and social distancing are often impossible in these areas, and health facilities are minimal.

While the majority of life-saving food assistance will be provided through in-kind food assistance, in areas where markets will be proven to be functional and retailers will have sufficient capacity, WFP will make use of commodity vouchers to deliver food assistance. projects.name: 3.1.1.5 - STRENGTHENING COMMUNITY POLICING IN CABO DELGADO, MOZAMBIQUE
projects.description:
The following activities are planned to strengthen community policing in Cabo Delgado:   
The overall objective of the project is to improve the security for the populations in the conflict-affected districts in Cabo Delgado through the reinforcement of community policing approaches.   
This long-term objective will be achieved through Outcome 1, which aims to ensure that the GoM security forces and community leaders are committed to implementing community policing initiatives. This commitment will be measured and considered as achieved by the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) or Letter of Agreement (LoA) between GoM security forces and community leaders which clearly states the intention to reinforce the implementation of community policing initiatives to contribute to increased security in Cabo Delgado. The outcome will be achieved through the delivery of three outputs.   
Output 1 ensures that baseline information on the current perceptions of the security situation and the response by the GoM security forces is available. In order to achieve this, it is important to have meetings and conversations with GoM security structures at the national, provincial and district levels to ensure that GoM buy-in is secured and that the GoM plays a leading role throughout the project implementation process. Furthermore, it is assumed that the communities in the conflict-affected districts have significant situational awareness and a strong understanding of the unidentified armed men in the area. Hence, this is a source of information that can be tapped to increase the understanding of the current security situation in Cabo Delgado. Information from the community level will also be collected through supporting the police with a mobile police stand to be in close proximity with the communities and to engage them. During this engagement, further information can be collected which will be helpful in establishing the baseline information. 

Output 2 will promote that GoM security forces, community leaders and representatives of the energy sector to have a common understanding of community policing. This is crucial, as a common understanding of the security situation in Cabo Delgado, with a special focus on the perception and knowledge of local community leaders, will be a stepping stone for any future security intervention that engages and closely cooperates with the conflict-affected communities. The relevant information will be presented in form of a baseline report as well as prepared into a table top exercise. 
The report and the table top exercise will be presented and conducted, respectively, at a workshop in Pemba. The workshop in Pemba will bring together all the relevant stakeholders from the GoM security forces from the national, provincial and district levels, the relevant local community leaders, including religious leaders, as well as relevant representatives from the energy sector. The workshop will not only present the findings from the baseline report and conduct the table top exercise, which will promote a common understanding of the attacks in Cabo Delgado as well as the response to the attacks, but it will also provide a space to discuss the advantages of the community policing approach, present experiences with community policing from other countries and reflect on how the private sector can positively contribute to promoting security for the populations in conflict-affected districts.
The above stated outcome will be further achieved through the implementation of Output 3. Output 3 states that GoM security forces and community leaders are willing to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) or a Letter of Agreement (LoA) to promote the implementation of community policing approaches. 
This commitment is important and crucial if community policing is to be an approach that will indeed be implemented. Therefore, a workshop will be conducted in Pemba which brings together key stakeholders and community leaders from the conflict-affected districts, as well as key representatives from the GoM security forces in order to sign a MoU or LoA. To promote as much as possible an inclusive approach is key and will be a determining factor of the success, or lack thereof, of any future community policing intervention. The signing of a MoU or LoA should also be accompanied by the discussion and agreement on some concrete future steps and needs in order to promote and implement community policing.

projects.name: 3.1.1.6 - PILOT PROJECT: FACILITATING LONG TERM SOLUTIONS FOR POST-CONFLICT PEACE CONSOLIDATION IN MOZAMBIQUE
projects.description:
The project aims at contributing to the provision of long term solutions for post-conflict peace consolidation in Mozambique.  
This shall be reached through:
(1) Conduct an assessment report on the basic profile of ex-combatants in order to inform viable solutions with regard to their reintegration. This will include basic profile information about combatants, such as their numbers, their ages, education levels, skills sets, capacity to generate an income, etc. The assessment will also include a social network analysis of RENAMO ex-combatants, to identify potential factions and cleavages within RENAMO. This is a necessary precursor to providing viable and appropriate responses to their requirements.
(2) Conduct an assessment of ex- combatants reintegration needs that will inform viable responses to pension requirements and other reintegration opportunities (income generating projects) needed for the reintegration of ex-combatants, enabling GoM and donors to plan more effectively future assistance needs. This assessment will also include a mapping of existing job-creation programs in the provinces, where ex-combatants will be reintegrated that have the capacity to absorb ex-combatants.
Both assessments will require quite a substantial amount of preparation and advocacy efforts, as both parties might have some reservations. The RENAMO leadership has been reluctant to identify the combatants that require recognition and assistance. The government might oppose to the idea to integrate more people into the pension system, as this will increase the costs of the state budget in time of increasing costs and less donor support.
(3) Provide technical support with regard to the reintegration of ex-combatants to the negotiating parties and donors to strengthen this critical element of the peace process and ensure its durability.
(4) Support income generation activities: On the basis of the assessment-activity 2, develop (grouped) pilot income generation initiatives and where possible integrate ex-combatants in ongoing income generating activities of other IOs and NGOs that were identified in the assessment. Limited pilot livelihood assistance options will include in-kind grants, small business start-up, on the job training to employment, vocational training to employment, business development service training, and referral to employment and integration in ongoing other job creation programs.

A baseline needs analysis of the trades to be offered will precede the program and this process will be imperative as it will provide the information required of trades or courses that will resonate to the labour market demands.
• Preparation of beneficiaries for skills training. 
YA´s experience with training, has shown that adolescents and young people who sell sex or engage in transactional sex, key beneficiaries of this proposed project are likely to fail in completing trainings. Based on this, all beneficiaries will undergo a training for transformation for a period of three weeks. 
• Centre based integral vocational training. 
After successful completion of the training for transformation, at least 720 young people identified will receive technical vocational education and training (TVET) at YA centres in Chitungwiza, Epworth (Zimbabwe) and Beira, (Mozambique). TVET will be integrated with Life Skills Education (LSE) and Entrepreneurship skills training
• Mobile outreach training. 
YA will seek to replicate the centre based integral vocational training model in the border towns of Chirundu, Beitbridge (Zimbabwe) and Cabo Delgado, Manica (Mozambique). The model will reach out to at least 390 young people including key populations such as sex workers and young people on the edge of migrating.
• Life skills Education. 
Life skills education is an integral and compulsory part of YA’s youth empowerment program. The aim of the life skills program is to empower young people with a range of soft skills that make them self -confident, responsible, fulfilled and purposeful citizens of their communities and thus live with dignity and purpose. 
• HIV sensitive case management.
All beneficiaries enrolled in the project will be case managed. Case management is a multi-step process to ensure timely access to and coordination of medical and psychosocial services for a person living with HIV based on the following process: intake, assessment of needs, service planning, service plan implementation, service coordination, monitoring and follow-up, reassessment, case conferencing and case closure. 
• Community Outreach Initiatives. 
The STOP AIDS (2016) report on adolescents and young people and HIV, revealed that a few young people with HIV are aware of their infection, the majority have never tested to know if they are infected. To redress this, YA will jointly with Frontline AIDS conduct community outreach initiatives which will take the form of festivals at YA centres, exhibitions, peer to peer conversations in public transport i.e. commuter omnibuses as well as sports galas. 
• Stakeholder engagement and Partnerships. 
The project will partner with Frontline AIDS, a HIV specialist organisation who will give oversight in implementation of all HIV interventions such as facilitation of HTS, ensuring beneficiaries are initiated on treatment, supported to adhere to their treatment and retained in support and care. 
The project will also incorporate a gender module in skills training programme as one of relevant cross cutting issue.

The project ‘Supporting Post Disaster Recovery Efforts through Climate Resilient Public Spaces In Cyclone Affected Areas’ will target in particular the City of Dondo, in Sofala Province, Mozambique, one of the most affected by Cyclone Idai. The city of Dondo is located 30 km from Beira, with about 130,000 inhabitants. It is a city with industrial, logistic and agricultural characteristics and one of the most important settlement of Beira Corridor. The urban centres of the Beira Corridor were highly impacted by the Tropical Cyclone IDAI, and Dondo was one of the most    impacted due the concentration of population, urban services and infrastructures.  
The main idea of the Project is that public spaces in the target city have the potential to be used in three main areas of disaster management: emergency response, recovery and reconstruction, by mainstreaming the resilient construction standards. The project will thus provide practical and easily replicable solutions that allow public spaces construction and improvement specifically fitted out for vulnerable communities, young girls and women. 
In particular one (1) resilient public space will be built in Dondo City to serve as a space for social integration in the city as well as safe haven in case of disaster.
The key component of the project’s implementation process is the community engagement, combining with programming and capacity building through a Participatory Public Spaces Design. Community members and especially vulnerable people (e.g. children, elders, young girls, women and disabled people) will constitute a core part of the effort to understand where public spaces   need to be developed, what kind of existing resources they provide and what are the underlying patterns  for how they are used.

projects.name: 4.2.2.25 - BRIGHT AND RESILIENT CLASSROOMS IN THE NAMACURRA DISTRICT Improving school and child resilience in Mozambique
projects.description:
The project proposal 'Light and Resilient Classrooms in Namacurra District' will be part of the existing and broader Safe Schools Programme, for which UN-Habitat has provided technical assistance to the Ministry of Education and Human Development (MINEDH), with funding from UNICEF, as will be explained in item III of this re-exam of the project proposal.

Currently, due to the lack of public electricity supply, school communities in Namacurra district are isolated and vulnerable in case of emergencies such as cyclones, winds and heavy rains. For example, there is a lack of energy for media integrated into an early warning system in the event of climatic calamities, which makes it difficult to prepare communities and which could prevent calamities such as human and economic losses. 
 
Under the 'A2E CSR Fund' programme, the UN-Habitat project proposal is to select four (4) school buildings already rebuilt by the Safe Schools Programme (see item III) and provide them with a renewable energy source, preferably solar panels. With this, the reconstructed and resilient classrooms will be transformed into safe learning infrastructures with the potential to become the reference point for the school community and its surroundings, as it will be able to provide energy to supply the means of communication and equipment of community members at alternative times. By providing a school building with an alternative and sustainable energy source, this project can thus strengthen the social, economic and environmental development of the surrounding community.
 
The introduction of alternative and sustainable energy into the school communities of Namacurra represents the opportunity to increase the educational offer and reach of the schools with: (i) more hours of teaching and evening courses for adults and young workers; (ii) installation of information and communication technologies (ICTs) for more effective teaching of children and young people; (iii) facilitating safe night access to schools for women and girls who need to work at home during the day. In addition, in surrounding communities, electricity could contribute to increasing access to information and communication media and devices, for example by including charging stations for mobile phones and radios.

projects.name: Reconnecting people with their place:enhance community potential for a resilient reconstruction after Idai in Beira, Mozambique
projects.description:
Tropical Cyclone Idai made landfall twice in Mozambique, first on 5 March affecting central and northern provinces of Mozambique including southern Malawi, and then during the night of 14 to 15 March 2019 through Beira City (530.000 people, badly affected, with most vulnerable neighbourhood having around 90% of building damaged or completely destroyed) and then moved North-West through Sofala and Manica Provinces, until reaching Zimbabwe where it died off.
Cyclone Idai is estimated to have affected almost 3 million people in the sub-region, primarily in Mozambique, but also with heavy losses in Zimbabwe and Malawi, leaving behind over 700 people dead, many thousands injured or isolated, over 150,000 people displaced, at least 100,000 houses damaged or entirely destroyed and an initial economical damages estimate to Key infrastructure and loss of livelihood of around 700mln USD. Currently thousands of cases of cholera and diarrhoea are being diagnosticated, which will possibly increase the number of victims even more. It is a disaster of epic proportions, probably the worst ever recorded in the region.
UN-Habitat reacted immediately to the humanitarian call and took over a pro-active role in the recovery process, as a key stakeholder in the humanitarian coordination, particularly in Shelter, Early Recovery and Education clusters, and formulating a Strategy to support response, recovery and resilient reconstruction in Mozambique as main instrument of coordination of its activities at country level. 
During its long-standing presence in Mozambique since 2002 with a young, dynamic and multi-sectorial country team, UN-Habitat worked particularly in DRR, adaptation to climate change and resilience and took part in several disaster recovery and reconstruction efforts that affected the country in the past (Zambesi Floods of 2002, 2007, 2009, Dineo Cyclone among the most relevant). 
In these years UN-Habitat has established also an excellent relationship with Beira Municipality, promoting participative approaches in slum upgrading to improve quality of life in the most vulnerable neighbourhoods of the city like Munhava. 
The Mayor of Beira counts on UN-Habitat strong support for re-building the city and is already promoting a reconstruction multi-stakeholder platform/taskforce to produce a Beira City Recovery and Resilient Reconstruction Plan - BRRRP (as a framework instrument to canalize all short and medium term humanitarian support efforts towards a more resilient city, ready to face future climatic challenges and stresses).
In post-disaster context normally stakeholders are driven by the necessity to assess and respond quickly, based on weak analysis, mainly done in a technocratic way, through a point of view that often relies on drones and satellites more than on people experience and know-how.
With this initiative UN-Habitat wants to promote a planning approach with the People at the centre of the process, showing how a strong community engagement since the initial response actions, linked strongly with the key-stakeholders platform for response and recovery, is the way to ensure a resilient reconstruction, especially in urban areas.
  

I.	OBJECTIVE
Within the above-mentioned Municipal framework of action (reconstruction platform/taskforce and BRRRP) and coherently with the UN-Habitat Post Disaster support Strategy, the project main objective is to engage and support the affected communities living in Beira most vulnerable neighborhoods to take active part in the process of recovery and reconstruction of their own settlements.
This aims at mobilizing the local knowledge of the settlers, to produce an exhaustive and critical analysis of the structural weakness and strengths of the neighborhood before, during and after the disaster, identifying damages per typology and relevance, their impact on the collective identity of the place, producing valuable contributions to the institutional reconstruction efforts, in terms of knowledge, prioritization and engagement. The community-based approach will ensure a faster and more efficient recovery and will provide opportunities to build back better and deploy local control over recovery.

projects.name: 2.3.3.19 - ASSESSING THE PROTECTION AND CHILD PROTECTION RISKS AND NEEDS IN CABO DELGADO, MOZAMBIQUE
projects.description:
Populations in Cabo Delgado have been experiencing overlapping challenges due to an increasing wave of insecurity recorded over the past two years. The humanitarian situation in Cabo Delgado has deteriorated rapidly in the first six months of 2020 due to insecurity and violence, compounded by climatic shocks. At least 195 violent incidents were reported between January and June 2020  [1] leading to a significant increase in displacement across the province and a consequent rise in protection risks for the most vulnerable people – including both those displaced and those who remained in insecure areas.  
This project aims to provide an evidence base for protection and child protection risks and needs in Cabo Delgado to inform humanitarian planning and to increase donor interest in addressing and mitigating the risks. Building on IOM’s presence and DTM capacity in Cabo Delgado, this project will lead to the availability of an assessment report on protection and child protection risks and needs in Cabo Delgado. In the long run, this will contribute to strengthening the prevention of and the response to neglect, abuse, exploitation, and violence against children in Cabo Delgado.

projects.name: 2.1.1.3 - Support school reconstruction within the emergency resilient recovery project framework
projects.description:
School reconstruction and piloting to develop models for schools that withstand natural hazards and mainstream the outcome into national rules and regulations  within the Emergency Resilient Recovery Project (ERRP) framework.

The global outcome of the project will be to make school communities more resilient and in a more secure environment, based on the development of capacities, knowledge appropriation and adoption of technical measures by stakeholders in the provinces of Zambézia, Nampula and Niassa. It is expected to capitalize the benefits of this reconstruction initiative – the first large-scale effort to be undertaken in the country – to lay foundations for future post-disaster recovery strategies and actions in Mozambique.   

The enhanced reconstruction initiative involves a series of scopes between them; institutional development and capacities, management and planning at central and provincial levels, transfer of technical capacities, as well as the adoption of good practices and lessons learned from international experiences in post-disaster areas. For this reason, the proposed Terms of Reference point the need of involve several partners from central to local level in order to ensure the implementation and execution of the project in its different phases, including the Academy. 

This initiative will gather the recommendations and benefits from the Safe School Project (GFDRR-MINEDH) as well as look for a strategic alignment with other projects that are taking place in the scope of the implementation of scholar structure such as (i) Accelerated Construction Project of Classrooms (PCA-FASE), (ii) the community-based pilot project for improved reconstruction being implemented in the province of Zambézia (district of Namacurra), as well as the implementation of (iii) Basic School Emergency Plan (PEBE), both projects count with the support of UNICEF and UN-Habitat technical assistance.  

As mentioned above, all the actions will be carried out under the institutional leadership of MINEDH through the National Directorate of Infrastructures and School Equipment (DIEE) in coordination with the provinces (Unit of the Sector of Infrastructures and School Equipment – UPCEE) and in partnership with MOPHRH, with emphasis on the National Directorate of Buildings (DNE) as one of the strategic partners to adopt the long-term gains of the project in the normative scope. All technical assistance derived from this consultancy will be offered and submitted to your leadership and guidance.

projects.name: 2.3.2.13 - UN-Habitat Building Back Better and Resilience Building Umbrella Programme-COVID 19 Response Emergency Fund
projects.description:
Objectives: Improve the health and living conditions of people in informal settlements tackling pre-emptive actions that will help in preventing and responding to the unfolding COVID 19 crisis in Mozambique, taking into consideration their complex and sensitive socio-economic patterns.
•	Problem being addressed: In Mozambique, 80% of the urban population live in informal settlements which are dense, overpopulated, with poor sanitation and public health conditions, and lack of access to basic services. The 2018 Afro-barometer survey indicates that up to 42% of urban households don’t have a water source inside their compounds, 13% don’t have a latrine or toilet and 28% don’t have electric supply or connection to the home. It is therefore very clear that there is a high risk that COVID 19's impacts on the urban poor living in informal settlements will be considerably high compared to other areas, as applying social distancing and self-isolation is more difficult in overcrowded areas with inadequate housing conditions. In addition, these populations do not have reliable economic mechanisms to support themselves for long periods of time without a regular/daily income. As the virus starts spreading in Mozambique we will inevitably see more and more people bearing severe health consequences, not just because of limited access to healthcare, access to basic services (water, sanitation, etc.) but also because they are forced to prioritize their economic needs and concerns over their health. It is therefore important to set up specific and concrete mechanisms to address the impacts of COVID-19 in the informal settlements as this pandemic will affect all income classes but most drastically and dis-proportionally the poorest ones. 
•	Integration into the broader COVID-19 response: This proposal is integrated within the UN-Habitat COVID-19 Prevention and Response Strategy for Mozambique and is fully aligned with the UN Mozambique Preparedness and Response Plan. It also leverages the existing efforts being deployed in the biggest urban centres of Mozambique (Maputo, Nampula, Beira and Dondo) in which the prevalence of informal settlements in high, within the scope of the UN-Habitat Building Back Better and Resilience Building Umbrella Programme promoting safer and resilient communities. The proposed action is well aligned with UN-Habitat Response and Recovery Strategy for sub-Saharan Africa and with UN-Habitat global strategy on COVID-19.
Expected output/results during the funding period: 
	Local Governments and Communities have enhanced capacities to reduce the COVID-19 spreading risk and its negative impacts in urban areas, particularly in informal settlements.
	Enhanced multi-sectoral coordination to effectively plan and monitor COVID-19 interventions in urban areas with focus on informal settlements.
	Slum dwellers are provided with the basic needs to face the unfolding crisis of COVID-19 while implementing the WHO’s recommendations to contain the spread of the virus and prevent contamination.
	The urban poor are covered by specific and contextualized COVID-19 prevention and response actions to reduce their vulnerabilities to contamination and spreading risk in their settlements.
Impact on beneficiaries: Local governments will be more prepared to apply an efficient, rapid and targeted response in informal settlements in terms of COVID-19 response and prevention measures.
